title: A Space Blast That Kept Flashing for 27 Days
summary:
Astronomers have found a space explosion that would not stop. The blast, called GRB 220706A, was first seen on July 6, 2022. Its central engine kept flashing in X-rays for around 27 days.

That beats the record for this kind of flashing, about six days, by around 20 days. Gamma-ray bursts, or GRBs, are some of the most powerful explosions in space.

Long GRBs happen when a huge star collapses. That collapse also causes a supernova and makes a black hole. GRB 220706A is an ultra-long GRB, a rare kind whose engine stays active for longer. Scientists still do not know what caused it.

Benjamin Gompertz, of the University of Birmingham in England, said flashing after a GRB is common, but it had always come in the first few days. Flashes at around 27 days show something is still powering the blast, he said.

One idea is a magnetar, a neutron star with a very strong magnetic field. The new supernova looks like the one linked to GRB 111209A, another ultra-long GRB from 2011 that was powered by a magnetar.
why_it_matters: It shows you that space can still surprise scientists, just like a mystery you keep solving can turn out longer and stranger than you first thought.

The leftover energy can keep glowing for a while as the explosion fades away.
